section_title: Circuit Consequences: Dendritic Inhibition, Oscillations, Sleep, and Memory
thesis: SST interneurons control the distal dendritic compartment and are required for low-gamma synchronisation, producing weaker and slower somatic suppression than PV cells but a larger reduction of gamma power when silenced. That functional signature is what makes a reduction in somatostatin signalling a dendritic-integration and oscillatory problem rather than a spike-threshold problem - and it explains why a disease can have a severe SST phenotype without a single SST neuron dying.
scope_notes: Circuit-level consequences: dendritic inhibition, oscillations, sleep, memory; bridge cellular findings to symptoms.

arg_01.thesis: The dendritic signature: what SST manipulation does that PV manipulation does not - Establish the strongest converging evidence in the review - three independent preparations, three methods, same direction, explicit effect sizes - that SST manipulation gives weaker/slower somatic effects and larger gamma reduction, consistent with dendritic targeting. subsections.title: The dendritic signature: what SST manipulation does that PV manipulation does not
subsections.job: Establish the strongest converging evidence in the review - three independent preparations, three methods, same direction, explicit effect sizes - that SST manipulation gives weaker/slower somatic effects and larger gamma reduction, consistent with dendritic targeting. subsections.title: Oscillatory phenotypes in disease models: band- and parameter-specific
subsections.job: Show that amyloid models reduce gamma power while a tau-propagation model preserves gamma peak frequency, and that pooling "gamma deficit" conflates amplitude with frequency. opening_constraint: Sections 4-7 produced apparently contradictory cellular descriptions of the same class; this section shows that most of them converge on one circuit-level prediction once dendritic targeting and peptidergic signalling are taken seriously.
closing_constraint: The circuit account makes predictions about human brain function. (sec-human-evidence) assembles the human postmortem, single-nucleus and fluid evidence that can test them, and finds the strongest and the weakest claims of the review side by side.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: SST-specific causal tests of oscillatory deficits in neurodegeneration models
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Cell-type-specific gain or loss of SST function inside amyloid or tau models with simultaneous measurement of gamma, theta and slow-oscillation power. Existing causal gamma manipulations target PV or broad GABAergic populations; the SST-specific causal experiment in a disease model was not found in this search.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The field infers an SST contribution to disease oscillopathy from SST circuit function in healthy animals plus SST loss in disease tissue, without closing the causal loop.

evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Direct recordings or manipulations of identified cortical SST interneurons during spindle events. Searches linking somatostatin interneurons to spindles returned studies of slow oscillations, NREM sleep onset and sleep-deprivation transcript changes, but no spindle-locked SST unit data.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Spindle density is one of the strongest human sleep correlates of tau burden, so the absence of SST-level mechanism leaves the human biomarker without a cellular interpretation.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Whether SST-mediated dendritic inhibition gates plasticity in human cortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Human tissue or in vivo human evidence for dendrite-targeted inhibitory gating of plasticity; all retrieved mechanistic evidence is rodent slice or rodent in vivo.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Section claims about dendritic inhibition in human neurodegeneration currently extrapolate across species without a bridging measurement.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: The claim that SST interneuron loss causes network hypersynchrony in Alzheimer disease
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration - claim is repeated across reviews but the original data source linking SST loss specifically (rather than PV dysfunction or general inhibitory failure) to hypersynchrony was not identified in this search.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: widely stated mechanistic claim without traceable experimental evidence; conversely one retrieved study localises amyloid-induced gamma failure to PV and not SST synapses.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Gamma entrainment as a therapeutic mechanism
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Replication of the amyloid-lowering effect of 40 Hz stimulation by laboratories outside the originating group, and reconciliation with evidence that flicker does not entrain endogenous gamma oscillators.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: A clinical-translation programme rests on a mechanism whose two premises - that flicker drives native gamma circuits and that doing so clears amyloid - are each contradicted by at least one retrieved study.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Direction of SST interneuron activity change in amyloid models in vivo
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: No study retrieved measures SST-cell firing and PV-cell firing with the same awake electrophysiological readout in both knock-in and transgenic amyloid models at matched ages; immediate-early-gene and spike-rate studies disagree in sign.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Circuit interpretations of dendritic disinhibition in Alzheimer models depend on whether SST cells are hypo- or hyperactive, and the current evidence cannot discriminate.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: SST-specific contribution to sleep spindles and slow oscillations in neurodegeneration
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Interventional sleep-rescue studies in disease models drive GABAergic interneurons broadly (opsins or zolpidem) rather than SST cells specifically; no retrieved study restores slow-wave activity by SST-selective manipulation in a tau or amyloid model.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Attributing sleep-oscillation rescue to dendritic inhibition requires cell-type-selective causal evidence that currently does not exist.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Primary experimental demonstration that dendritic SST inhibition gates plasticity in behaving animals
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration - claim is repeated across reviews but the original in vivo data source linking OLM/SST dendritic inhibition to behaviourally relevant plasticity gating was identified only in slice and head-fixed imaging preparations.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: widely stated claim without traceable experimental evidence in freely behaving animals.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Whether SST interneuron number is actually reduced in disease models versus functionally impaired
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Head-to-head stereology of SST+ populations across amyloid, tau and synucleinopathy models at matched ages; the one unbiased stereological study retrieved reports no SST+ loss in a transgenic AD rat, while density-based studies report decline.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Circuit accounts of dendritic disinhibition differ depending on whether SST cells are absent or present but dysfunctional, and counting methodology alone may explain part of the literature's disagreement.

certified_evidence_limits.search_coverage: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval. certified_evidence_limits.fulltext_shortfall_concentration: The shortfall is concentrated in pre-2000 closed-access postmortem and CSF literature (radioimmunoassay series), which is recorded at abstract level only. certified_evidence_limits.disconfirming_sweeps: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. Negative-result and conflict coverage is a top-relevance sample, not a census. certified_evidence_limits.conflict_axis_labels_provisional: Axes were assigned by a documented rule applied to the recorded nature_of_conflict text. Five candidate axes (measurement modality and what was counted; species, region and circuit context; model construct and species transfer; cohort composition, stage and comorbidity; design rigor and statistical unit) were keyword-scored, with the region/species axis down-weighted (0.55) because regional context is named in almost every conflict record, and design rigor up-weighted (1.3) because it is named rarely and only when it is the point. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. These tags are a planning classification derived from the conflict text, not a measurement; the writing phase should correct any tag that misreads a conflict, and the atlas figure must state that conflicts can appear in more than one axis row.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_inventory_caveat: This inventory is the set of disagreements recorded during a search whose disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. It is a top-relevance sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and no rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Whether SST circuits are spared in amyloid-oligomer-induced oscillopathy. The first localises dysfunction to pyramidal-cell-to-PV synapses with PC-to-SST synapses intact; the second reports amyloid-oligomer-induced depression of SST as well as PV interneuron-evoked inhibition together with reduced theta and gamma power in SST-Cre mice. The dimension of disagreement is whether the SST pathway is functionally affected, which may reflect input (PC-to-interneuron) versus output (interneuron-to-PC) synapses.

Whether 40 Hz sensory stimulation engages endogenous gamma oscillators or merely adds a stimulus-locked response. One reports increased 40 Hz spectral power across sleep stages as evidence of evoked gamma activity; the other shows that flicker cannot phase-capture endogenous narrow-band gamma, implying evoked power is an added steady-state response rather than entrainment of the native oscillator.

Direction of interneuron activity change in amyloid mouse cortex: one study reports hyperactivity of both PV and SST interneurons (elevated c-Fos) in App NL-G-F mice, while the other reports a shift of fast-spiking interneurons toward low-frequency firing (hypoactivity) in awake young APP/PS1 mice with unchanged pyramidal firing. The dimension of disagreement is the sign of interneuron activity change, confounded by model (knock-in vs transgenic), age, and readout (immediate-early gene expression vs extracellular spike rate).
